comentarios.texto: WHAT: the public members endpoint takes limit straight from params with no upper bound or positivity check. WHY: any visitor can request limit=1000000 and force serialization of every member of large groups, including automatic trust-level groups. A negative limit produces a PostgreSQL error (500). HOW: clamp limit to a sane range.

hist.text: groups_controller.rb:22-26 does take limit from params without a bound, but before the PR non-automatic groups returned all members with no limit and automatic groups already used an unbounded params[:limit]; the PR adds a default of 50 and paginates, so it does not introduce the unbounded read.

The changed endpoint passes the integer limit directly into the query and serializes its results without bounds checks (app/controllers/groups_controller.rb:22–29), allowing oversized responses and PostgreSQL errors for negative limits. Visible groups are accessible anonymously (lib/guardian.rb:120–121); although automatic groups already accepted unchecked limits, this PR extends that behavior to nonautomatic groups.

Keep FP none. The PR adds a bound rather than removing one. At base, groups_controller.rb applied `members.limit(limit).offset(offset)` only `if group.automatic?`, and every non-automatic group serialized ALL members with no limit at all (`render_serialized(members.to_a, GroupUserSerializer)`). At head (:22-26) `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` paginates every group. So `limit=1000000` returns no more than a plain request did before, and the unchecked params[:limit] for automatic groups (including negative values) is carried over unchanged from base (`(params[:limit] || 200).to_i`). The PR only shrinks the default exposure; it introduces no oversize or unbounded read.

Keep TP, specifically for negative limits newly affecting nonautomatic groups. At base, those groups ignored params[:limit]; at head, groups_controller.rb:22–26 unconditionally applies it, so limit=-1 now reaches PostgreSQL and produces a 500 during serialization. The reviewer correctly identifies oversized responses and unchecked limits on automatic groups as pre-existing, but that does not eliminate the newly introduced failure for nonautomatic groups.
